about: Code tables of the message header analysis of Graph Connectivity Tests (web demo and PowerShell tool). Sources: the public Microsoft documentation on the anti-spam message headers of Microsoft 365 (Exchange Online Protection, Defender for Office 365) and RFC 7208 (SPF), RFC 7489 (DMARC), RFC 8601 (Authentication-Results), RFC 8617 (ARC). Values marked observed are seen in real messages but not documented by Microsoft.

ARC.name: ARC
ARC.text: Authenticated Received Chain fields of the message.

CAT.name: Category
CAT.text: The protection policy that was applied to the message.

CIP.name: Connecting IP
CIP.text: The IP address that connected to Microsoft 365.

CTRY.name: Country
CTRY.text: The country or region of the connecting IP address.

H.name: HELO
H.text: The HELO or EHLO name the connecting server sent.

IPV.name: IP reputation
IPV.text: Reputation of the connecting IP address.

LANG.name: Language
LANG.text: Language the message is written in.

PTR.name: Reverse DNS
PTR.text: The PTR record of the connecting IP address.

SCL.name: Spam confidence level
SCL.text: -1 skipped, 0-1 not spam, 5-6 spam, 7-9 high confidence spam.

SFTY.name: Safety
SFTY.text: The message was found to be phishing.

SFV.name: Spam filtering verdict
SFV.text: What spam filtering did with the message.

SRV.name: Service
SRV.text: SRV:BULK - the message was marked as bulk by its bulk complaint level.

SFS.name: Spam rules
SFS.text: Spam filtering rules that matched (internal identifiers).

SFP.name: Spam filtering policy
SFP.text: SFP:1501 - the message was sent with the outbound spam policy limit.

X-CustomSpam.name: Advanced spam filter
X-CustomSpam.text: An advanced spam filter (ASF) option of the anti-spam policy matched.

EFV.name: Internal
EFV.text: Internal value of the filtering service.

dir.INB: inbound: from the Internet or an external organisation
dir.OUT: outbound: sent by the organisation to the Internet
dir.INT: internal: between mailboxes of the same organisation

BLK.text: Spam filtering was skipped and the message was blocked: the sender is in the Blocked Senders list of the mailbox.

NSPM.text: Spam filtering found the message clean: it goes to the recipients.

SFE.text: Spam filtering was skipped and the message allowed: the sender is in the Safe Senders list of the mailbox.

SKA.text: Spam filtering was skipped and the message allowed: the sender is in an allowed senders or allowed domains list of an anti-spam policy.

SKB.text: The message was marked as spam: the sender is in a blocked senders or blocked domains list of an anti-spam policy.

SKI.text: Internal message of the organisation (intra-organisation): spam filtering was skipped.

SKN.text: The message was marked non-spam before spam filtering, usually by a mail flow rule (SCL -1).

SKQ.text: The message was released from quarantine and sent to the recipients.

SKS.text: The message was marked as spam before spam filtering, usually by a mail flow rule.

SPM.text: Spam filtering marked the message as spam.

cat.FTBP: Anti-malware filtered attachment types (common attachment filter)

ipv.CAL: Spam filtering was skipped: the IP address is in the IP Allow List of the connection filter policy.
ipv.NLI: The IP address is not on any IP reputation list.

sfty.9.19: Domain impersonation: the sending domain tries to look like a domain of the organisation or a protected domain.
sfty.9.20: User impersonation: the sender tries to look like a protected user of the organisation.

scl.text: Spam filtering was skipped (allow list, mail flow rule, or an internal message).
Not spam: delivered to the Inbox.
Not spam (these values are not used by Microsoft 365).
Spam: the action of the anti-spam policy for spam applies (Junk Email folder by default).
High confidence spam: the action for high confidence spam applies.
High confidence spam: the action for high confidence spam applies.

bcl.text: Bulk mail from a sender with few complaints.
Bulk mail from a sender with a mixed number of complaints.
Bulk mail from a sender with many complaints.

results.pass: Composite authentication passed: Microsoft 365 trusts the sender of the From address.
results.fail: Composite authentication failed: Microsoft 365 treats the From address as spoofed.
results.none: Composite authentication was not evaluated or was bypassed.

reasons.text: Explicit failure: DMARC failed and the domain of the From address asks receivers to quarantine or reject (p=quarantine or p=reject).
Implicit failure: the domain of the From address publishes no DMARC (or a weak) policy, and Microsoft 365 found the message not trustworthy (SPF, DKIM, sender history).
The organisation forbids this sender and domain pair to spoof (Tenant Allow/Block List or spoof intelligence).
DMARC failed with p=quarantine or p=reject for a domain that is an accepted domain of the organisation (self-to-self or intra-organisation spoofing).
The ARC result of a trusted sealer overrode the DMARC failure.
The message passed composite authentication (the last two digits are internal codes).
Implicit authentication passed softly (soft pass): no explicit failure, but no full trust either.
The message was not checked for composite authentication.
Composite authentication was bypassed (for example an allow entry or a mail flow rule).
Implicit failure for a domain that is an accepted domain of the organisation.
Composite authentication was skipped because of a configuration of the organisation.

pass.text: The sending IP address is allowed by the SPF record of the MAIL FROM domain.

fail.text: The SPF record of the MAIL FROM domain refuses the sending IP address (-all).

softfail.text: The SPF record of the MAIL FROM domain does not allow the sending IP address (~all).

neutral.text: The SPF record of the MAIL FROM domain says nothing about the sending IP address (?all).

none.text: The MAIL FROM domain has no SPF record.

temperror.text: A temporary DNS error prevented the SPF check.

permerror.text: The SPF record is broken: syntax error, more than 10 DNS lookups, or several SPF records.

fail.text: The DKIM signature did not verify: the message was changed in transit, or the key in DNS does not match.

none.text: The message is not signed with DKIM.

neutral.text: The DKIM signature could not be checked.

policy.text: The DKIM signature is valid but not accepted by the policy of the receiver.

temperror.text: A temporary DNS error prevented the DKIM check.

permerror.text: The DKIM signature or its key is broken (no key in DNS, bad syntax).

pass.text: DMARC passed: SPF or DKIM passed for a domain aligned with the From address.

bestguesspass.text: The domain of the From address has no DMARC record; the message would have passed if it had one.

fail.text: DMARC failed: neither SPF nor DKIM passed for a domain aligned with the From address.

none.text: The domain of the From address has no DMARC record.

temperror.text: A temporary DNS error prevented the DMARC check.

permerror.text: The DMARC record of the domain is broken.

dmarcAction.none: no action asked by the DMARC policy (p=none), or DMARC passed
dmarcAction.pct.quarantine: the policy asks for quarantine, but the message was outside the pct= sample
dmarcAction.pct.reject: the policy asks for reject, but the message was outside the pct= sample
dmarcAction.quarantine: the DMARC policy asks for quarantine (p=quarantine)
dmarcAction.reject: the DMARC policy asks for reject (p=reject)
dmarcAction.oreject: the DMARC policy asks for reject, Microsoft 365 applied its own action (the message was accepted and treated as spam or quarantined)
dmarcAction.bestguesspass: no DMARC record: best guess pass

fields.ucf: User custom flags (observed: 1 when a user setting or rule was involved).
fields.jmr: Junk mail rule of the mailbox (observed: 1 when the junk email rule of the mailbox acted).
fields.auth: Authentication of the sender for the mailbox (observed).
fields.dest: Destination folder chosen for the message in the mailbox.

dest.C: a custom folder (an inbox rule moved it)

CustomRules.text: An inbox rule of the mailbox (Outlook rule) decided the folder.

ExclusiveSettings.text: The Blocked Senders list or the Safe Senders list of the mailbox decided the folder.

SpamFilterAuthJ.text: The spam verdict of the service (SCL or failed sender authentication) sent the message to the Junk Email folder.

TrustedSenderList.text: The Safe Senders list of the mailbox kept the message in the Inbox.

Junk.text: The junk email filter of the mailbox moved the message.

Internal.text: The message was authenticated as coming from inside the organisation (a mailbox, a recognised on-premises server or connector).

Anonymous.text: The message came anonymously, as any message from the Internet.

Partner.text: The message came through a partner connector (TLS with a recognised partner).

External.text: The message was authenticated as external.

fromEntity.HybridOnPrem: the on-premises organisation of the hybrid (recognised through the inbound connector)
fromEntity.Internet: the Internet (not attributed to the organisation)

directionality.Incoming: received by the organisation from outside (incoming)
